newsitem.title: USA: U.S. doctors urge ban on land mines.
newsitem.headline: U.S. doctors urge ban on land mines.

text.p: A group of doctors on Saturday urged the Clinton administration to take part in a Canadian-led effort to negotiate a treaty banning anti-personnel land mines.

"The United States should join the countries who are willing to sign a ban on these weapons this year," said Dr. William Kennedy Smith, president of Physicians Against Land Mines, at a news conference jointly sponsored with the American Medical Association.
According to anti-land mine activists, about 26,000 people each year are killed or maimed worldwide by land mine explosions, and 80 percent are civilians.
"The AMA's concern is for the lives of those who live within a footstep of death," said Dr. Percy Wootton, president-elect of the AMA.
Last December, members of the AMA passed a resolution calling for the United States to join the other countries that have agreed to an immediate ban on the manufacture, sale and use of land mines.
Instead of participating in the Canadian talks which begin next week, the United States is supporting a U.N. effort to ban land mines that seeks to include other countries such as China and Russia.

"This is a prescription for non-action and will only hinder the signing of the treaty, because any country can hold up negotiations of the CD (U.N. Conference for Disarmament) by exercising their veto," said Representative Lane Evans, an Illinois Democrat who is on the House Veterans Affairs Committee.
The call for a ban on land mines came on the eve of the AMA's House of Delegates meeting, the major policy-making session for the group.
